AUTHOR: Fos Serdà
TITLE: Using Deep Neural Networks to Detect and Track Fish in Underwater Video Sequences
DATA: Luderick-Seagrass dataset (Ditria et al. 2021), pre-extracted 1920x1080 frames at 5 fps; 9,304 Luderick annotations after removing 125 Bream
D2: predefined Luderick-Seagrass split 6,702/1,661/1,066 annotations (Table I); unit not stated
D_EV: Sec. IV.A: 'The dataset is split in three parts ready to be used as training, validation and test sets. Table I shows information about each split.'
R_EV: Sec. IV.A: 'the Luderick-Seagrass dataset [22] has been used' (validation and test splits of that single dataset only)
C_EV: no statement found (only IoU thresholds and standard NMS described; no confidence threshold, FP verification, or ID-switch handling)
E_EV: Tables II–IV and Sec. IV.C: only mAP@0.5, mAP@0.75, mAP@0.5:0.05:0.95 and inference fps reported; tracking evaluated only by frame rate ('Results show a good fish tracking at the cost of a reduced frame rate').
ARCH: Faster R-CNN, YOLOv5 (s/m/l), Mask R-CNN detectors; SORT tracker on YOLOv5s detections
NOTE: Benchmark of detectors on the public Luderick-Seagrass dataset; tracking (SORT) is implemented but evaluated only qualitatively/by speed, so TYPE=검출. PLAT/ENV=NR because the paper gives no platform or habitat description beyond the dataset name and the reference title ('unconstrained seagrass habitats'); the original dataset is unbaited fixed cameras in Queensland estuarine seagrass — verify if the review wants dataset-derived values. NIMG=null: Table I gives annotation counts (9,420), not image counts. D1=predefined public split; the paper reports split sizes (Table I) but not the split unit of the original dataset (frames extracted at 5 fps from videos; original split unit unknown to coder), so D_ALL=P is per the 'predefined split stated' clause — a verifier may lower to N if the original split is frame-level random. PR curves are drawn across IoU thresholds, not confidence thresholds, so C4=N and C1=NR. Code and annotated video sequences at github.com/RicardFos/tfm_object_detection.
